description: Domain events Campbooks publishes (ADR 0012, ADR 0013): the triggers automation rules listen to and the inputs projections read. Generated from the modules' DomainEvent types; do not edit.

payload.description: An item opened, changed, cleared, or was snoozed or unsnoozed.

container.description: Who may see it: its container (`conversations.inbox`).

payload.description:
A calendar change ended
(`contracts/connectors.calendar_change_completed.v1.schema.json`).

calendar.description: The calendar (an id of the schedule module).

event.description: The event (an id of the schedule module).

provider_event_id.description: The event's id at the provider (applied only; opaque).

oneOf.description: Why it did not apply.

request.description: The request (an id of the schedule module).

payload.description:
A calendar stream produced a `calendar-change-batch` for one provider
calendar (`contracts/connectors.calendar_changed.v1.schema.json`).
Published in the transaction that advances the stream's cursor; the
schedule module applies it. Declared with the contract, published by the
Google Calendar adapter (campbooks-cloud#42).

batch.description: The `calendar-change-batch` v1 document, a blob of the workspace.

payload.description:
A connection gained a capability: a new connection, or an incremental
consent. For `messages` it names the inbox this module minted; the
conversations module creates it, with `granted_by` as its manager
(`contracts/connectors.capability_granted.v1.schema.json`).

account.description: The account's address and name: an [`AccountDocument`] blob.

oneOf.description: The inbox the stream feeds (`messages` only).

payload.description:
A member connected an outside account, or connected it again (a
reconnect, or the same account consenting anew: `refreshed`). Published
in the transaction that stores the grant, so whoever handed the grant
over can tell which connection it became even if its own request died.

account_subject.description:
The provider's stable id of the account (`sub`; opaque, never an
address).

grantor_subject.description:
The grantor as the identity module knows them (the token subject the
grant was handed over for).

refreshed.description: An existing connection got this grant (it was not created now).

payload.description:
A connection's grant stopped working (revoked, expired, or its stored
credentials can no longer be read): the member must connect again.

granted_by.description: The member who granted it, who can grant it again.

payload.description:
A connection was disconnected: its grant is revoked and its streams are
gone. `mail` says what becomes of the inboxes it fed
(`contracts/connectors.connection_removed.v1.schema.json`): the
conversations module deletes them, or keeps them read-only.

account_subject.description:
The provider's stable id of the account (the `OpenID` `sub`; opaque, never
an address), so a way in that came only from this connection can be
dropped with it.

oneOf.description: The member who had connected it.

mail.description: Delete the mail it brought in (the default), or keep it read-only.

oneOf.description: Its provider.

payload.description:
A messages stream produced a `MessageChangeBatch` for an inbox
(`contracts/connectors.messages_changed.v1.schema.json`). Published in
the transaction that advances the stream's cursor.

batch.description: The `MessageChangeBatch` v1 document, a blob of the workspace.

cursor.description: The stream's cursor after this batch (opaque, never personal data).

inbox_id.description: The conversations inbox; equals the batch's `inbox`.

payload.description:
A send asked for by `conversations.send_requested` ended
(`contracts/connectors.send_completed.v1.schema.json`). Ids only.

inbox_id.description: The inbox it was sent from.

provider_message_id.description: The provider's id of the sent message (sent only).

reason.description:
Why it failed (failed only): `not_connected`, `needs_reauth`,
`rejected`, `too_large`, `unavailable` (nothing was sent) or
`unknown_outcome` (it may have been).

payload.description:
A member (or automation, or the assistant, through an operation) asked
for changes the provider should make too: the connector's outbound work.
Never published for changes that came from the provider.

inbox_id.description: The inbox the messages belong to.

origin.description: Always `user`: changes from the provider produce no request.

payload.description: A conversation's state changed.

provider_message_ids.description:
The provider ids of the messages the change applies to, for carrying a
member's change to the provider.

oneOf.description: The state afterwards; `None` once the conversation is gone.

payload.description:
A draft was sent: the provider accepted it and the draft is gone. The
message itself arrives like any other (`message_sent`).

oneOf.description: The draft's author; `None` for a client token's draft.
The conversation it answered, if any.

payload.description:
The connection-account v1 document, as this module reads it
(`contracts/connection-account.v1.schema.json`).
The inbox changed in a way that may change who sees it, or what they
may do there: a member was given it, a membership ended, its owner
left, or it was kept read-only after its connection was removed. Ids
only.

The inbox was deleted with everything in it (its connection was removed
and its mail not kept). Ids only.

A read of a message was stored, of either layer
(`contracts/conversations.message_read.v1.schema.json`). The schedule
module turns its items into events and the tasks module its asks into
tasks. Ids, enums, keys and times only: no title, place, quote or amount
(a reader fetches them through `conversations.get_message_read`).

asks.description: The obligations of the reader, at most three.

items.description: The things that happen at a time, at most five.

oneOf.description:
The inbox's personal owner: the one member who reads it. None for a
shared inbox.

summary_ready.description: Whether the read holds a summary of the message.

oneOf.description:
The titles, places and calendar `UID`s of the items, by key: a
`read-texts` v1 document, a blob of the workspace that the message
holds (deleted with it). The schedule module reads it to name the
events it makes; the event log never holds the text.

payload.description: An inbound message was stored for the first time.

An outbound message was stored for the first time (sent from the
provider's own client today; from Campbooks once sending lands).

A conversation's need changed: it opened, changed, or was cleared.
Ids, enums and a date only (`contracts/conversations.need_changed.v1.schema.json`).

oneOf.description: Why it was cleared.
The member who cleared it, when one did.

inbox.description: The inbox: who may see the need.

oneOf.description:
The conversation's newest inbound message: when it changes, the
sender wrote again (a member's Later ends) even if the need did not.

message.description: The inbound message the need comes from.

oneOf.description: The need, or `None` once cleared.

revision.description:
Grows with every change of this conversation's need; apply only
newer ones (deliveries are not ordered).

payload.description:
Scout's summary of the email behind a conversation's need was written
(campbooks-cloud#204). Ids only: never the summary. It exists so open
Home items and readers ask for the conversation again and show it.

inbox.description: The inbox: who may see the conversation.

payload.description:
A taught rule or its run changed (no other module consumes it; its schema
is in `openapi/events.json`).
Ids, enums and counts only: never its conditions, the member's words or
an address.

inbox.description: The inbox: who may see the rule.

oneOf.description: Its current run, when it has one.

payload.description: A send failed: the draft is editable again and says why.

oneOf.description: The draft's author; `None` for a client token's draft.

payload.description:
A member's send left its undo window: the connector's outbound work
(`contracts/conversations.send_requested.v1.schema.json`). The message
is an outgoing-message v1 blob; the event carries ids only.

oneOf.description:
The draft's author; `None` for a client token's draft. Its change
reaches only them (a draft is private).

inbox_id.description: The inbox it is sent from.

message.description: The outgoing-message v1 document, a blob of the workspace.

send_id.description: This send: unique, the connector records it once.

payload.description: A person created an account (with its first way in).

provider.description: The provider of its first way in.

payload.description:
An administrator suspended an account: its sessions ended and its
refresh tokens were revoked, and it cannot sign in until it is
unsuspended. Consumers drop whatever else keeps it signed in (the web
BFF's sessions) and stop whatever acts in its name (the rules its
member taught).

at.description:
When the suspension took effect, read under the account's lock: a
later suspension or lift of the same account always has a later
`at`. Absent on events published before it existed (use the event's
`occurred_at`).

seq.description:
The account's count of suspensions and lifts, this one included
(odd: suspended). Of two changes to one account, the higher `seq` is
the later, whatever the clock said. Absent on events published
before it existed (order those by `at`).

payload.description:
An administrator lifted an account's suspension: it may sign in again.
Nothing that the suspension ended comes back, but what was only paused
(the rules its member taught) acts again.

at.description: When the lift took effect, ordered like [`AccountSuspended::at`].

seq.description:
The account's count of suspensions and lifts, this one included
(even: not suspended), ordered like [`AccountSuspended::seq`]. Absent
on events published before it existed.

payload.description: A workspace registered a client of its own.
A workspace removed a client of its own; its tokens no longer work.

A person allowed a client (in a workspace, unless it is Campbooks' own
app).

workspace.description: The workspace its tokens are bound to.

payload.description:
A consent ended (revoked by the person, or because they left the
workspace, or it was deleted); the client's tokens for them stop
working.

workspace.description: The workspace its tokens were bound to.

payload.description:
A spent authorization code or a rotated refresh token was presented
again; every token of that sign-in was revoked.

account.description: The account whose tokens were revoked.

client.description: The client they were issued to.

payload.description: A person signed in to the issuer.

provider.description: The provider, for a provider sign-in.

payload.description:
A person signed out everywhere: every issuer session of the account
ended and every refresh token it held was revoked. The web BFF ends its
own sessions of the account on it.
An account gained a way in: a provider identity or a passkey.

provider.description: The provider, for a provider identity.

way_in.description:
The provider identity or passkey added (absent from events published
before it was recorded).

payload.description: An account lost a way in.

provider.description: The provider, for a provider identity.

payload.description:
A provider calendar was turned on or off for the member. Connectors reads
a calendar turned on again from the start, and stops reading one turned
off (`contracts/schedule.calendar_sync_changed.v1.schema.json`).

connection.description: The connection whose calendar it is.

payload.description:
An event was cancelled, removed or deleted. Expanding the occurrences
of a series publishes nothing.

ends.description: When it ends, in the same form, if it has an end.

kind.description: What kind of dated thing it is.

owner.description: The member whose calendar it is.

oneOf.description: The record it was read from, if any (an email).

starts.description:
When it starts: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, or a
`YYYY-MM-DD` date when it is all-day.

payload.description:
An event changed: its time, its kind, its calendar, or the provider's
version replaced the member's.

ends.description: When it ends, in the same form, if it has an end.

kind.description: What kind of dated thing it is.

owner.description: The member whose calendar it is.

oneOf.description: The record it was read from, if any (an email).

starts.description:
When it starts: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, or a
`YYYY-MM-DD` date when it is all-day.

payload.description:
An event was added to a calendar: made by the member, read by Scout
from an email, or applied from a provider's batch.

ends.description: When it ends, in the same form, if it has an end.

kind.description: What kind of dated thing it is.

owner.description: The member whose calendar it is.

oneOf.description: The record it was read from, if any (an email).

starts.description:
When it starts: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, or a
`YYYY-MM-DD` date when it is all-day.

payload.description:
A member's change of an event on a provider calendar, for connectors to
make there (`contracts/schedule.outbound_requested.v1.schema.json`). The
text to write, the provider's ids and the etag the change was made
against travel in the blob, a `calendar-change` v1 document: the ids of a
calendar can be an address. Connectors asks the schedule module to
confirm the request through the kernel's calendar-requests port before it
acts.

body.description: The `calendar-change` v1 document, a blob of the workspace.

calendar.description: The calendar the event is on.

connection.description: The connection whose grant makes the change.

request.description: This request: unique, the connector records it once.

payload.description:
A user became a member: by creating the workspace or accepting an
invitation.
A user stopped being a member: they left, or were removed.

mail.description:
What becomes of the mail of the mailboxes they connected: deleted
(always when they leave), or kept read-only when the owner or admin
removing them chose so.

oneOf.description: Who removed them; `None` when they left.

subject.description:
Their identity subject (an opaque account id), so the issuer can
remove the clients they registered in the workspace.

payload.description: A member's role changed.

A member's account was suspended (`identity.account_suspended`): they
cannot get in, and whatever acts in their name in the workspace stops
until the suspension is lifted. Published in every workspace they belong
to.

at.description:
When the suspension took effect; orders the change only when it
carries no `seq`.

seq.description:
The account's count of suspensions and lifts as of this change
(identity's `seq`): of two changes to one member, the higher `seq`
is the truth, whatever order they arrive in. Absent when the change
came from an event published before it existed: such a change is
older than any that carries one, and two of them are ordered by `at`.

payload.description:
A member's suspension was lifted (`identity.account_unsuspended`).
Published in every workspace they belong to.

at.description: When the lift took effect, ordered like [`MemberSuspended::at`].

seq.description:
The account's count of suspensions and lifts as of this change,
ordered like [`MemberSuspended::seq`].

payload.description: A workspace was created; its creator is its first owner.

A workspace was deleted. Every module purges its data for it; the
workspace's own records are purged at `purge_after`.

A workspace setting changed (its name or its colour). Carries which
settings changed, never their values.

BlobPointer.description:
The schema of a stored blob reference (`campbooks_kernel::blobs::BlobRef`)
as it appears in events and documents: read the bytes with
`BlobStore::get` in the event's workspace.

content_type.description: The media type recorded with it.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the bytes, 64 lower-case hex digits.

BlobRef.description: How a [`BlobRef`] looks on the wire, for the events catalogue.

content_type.description: The media type given when it was stored.

hash.description: SHA-256 of the bytes, 64 lower-case hex digits.

CalendarChange.description: The change connectors is asked to make at the provider.

CalendarOutcome.description: How a calendar change asked for by `schedule.outbound_requested` ended.

CalendarReason.description:
Why a calendar change did not apply: a closed set, never the provider's
words.

Capability.description: What a connection lets Campbooks do with the account.

Channel.description: A kind of messaging. Email is the first.

ConversationState.description: A conversation's state after a change.

archived.description: Whether no message is in the inbox.

trashed.description: Whether every message is in the trash or spam.

EventKind.description:
What kind of dated thing an event is. A fixed set: obligations (pay by,
submit by, renew by) are never events, they are asks owned by `tasks`.

ItemKind.description:
What kind of thing that happens at a time a read of a message found
(campbooks-cloud#42). Obligations are not items: they are asks.

MailChoice.description:
What becomes of the mail a connection brought in when it is removed
(the owner's decision, campbooks-cloud#117): deleted with it (the
default), or kept as read-only history. Only the member who connected
it chooses when disconnecting; an owner or admin chooses when removing
that member.

MessageFacts.description:
Facts about one message, shared by [`MessageReceived`] and
[`MessageSent`].

provider_message_id.description: The provider's id for it, unique within the inbox.

stream.description: The conversation's stream when the message was stored.

oneOf.description: The plain-text body, when there is one.

NeedFacts.description: What a conversation needs, as `need_changed` carries it.

due_on.description: When it is due, when the message names a date that resolves.

lapses_at.description:
When what it asks stops being possible, as Scout read the email
(campbooks-cloud#275). Absent from events written before.

trust.description: How much Campbooks stands behind it.

NeedReason.description: Why a conversation needs its inbox's members (attention).

NeedTrust.description: How much Campbooks stands behind a need.

ReadAskFacts.description:
An ask of a stored read, as `message_read` carries it: its key, verb and
due, never its title, quote or amount.

due.description: By when: a date, or an RFC 3339 time with an offset.

has_amount.description: Whether the read holds an amount (the amount itself is not here).

key.description: Stable for the same message, layer and position.

same_as.description: The reference of an open task it repeats.

ReadItemFacts.description:
An item of a stored read, as `message_read` carries it: its key, kind and
times, never its title, place or quote.

cancels.description: The key of an earlier item of the conversation that it cancels.

ends.description: When it ends, in the same form.

key.description: Stable for the same message, layer and position.

kind.description: What kind of thing it is.

starts.description:
When it starts: an RFC 3339 time with an offset, or a date when
all-day.

time_zone.description: Its IANA time zone, when the message gave one.

updates.description: The key of an earlier item of the conversation that it changes.

ReadLayer.description:
Which reader produced a read: the sender's own machine-readable data,
or Scout's one `complete` call.

id.description: The record's id within its module.

RequestOrigin.description: Who asked for a requested change.

oneOf.description: Mark the message read.
Mark the message unread.
Star (flag) the message.
Unstar the message.
Take the message out of the inbox.
Put the message back in the inbox.
Move the message to the trash.
Take the message out of the trash, back where it was.

inbound.description:
It is mail the inbox received (not the member's own): where a
provider cannot tell where it was, it goes back to the inbox.

oneOf.description: Report the message as spam (move it to the spam folder).

Take the message out of spam: mail the inbox received goes back to
the inbox, the member's own mail is only taken out of spam.

inbound.description: It is mail the inbox received (not the member's own).

oneOf.description: Put a label on the message.

provider_key.description: The provider's key for it, when the provider already has it.

oneOf.description: Take a label off the message.

provider_key.description: The provider's key for it, when the provider has it.

oneOf.description:
The conversation was moved to another stream (providers with their
own categories may mirror it; others ignore it).

RequestedChange.description: A change a member asked for, to be made at the provider too.

RequestedItem.description: One message and the change asked for it.

provider_message_id.description: The provider's id for the message.

Role.description: A member's role in a workspace.

RunFacts.description: A taught rule's run, as `rule_changed` carries it: counts only.

kind.description: Applying the rule, or putting back what it changed.

RunKind.description: What a run over existing mail does.

Stream.description:
The one place Campbooks sorts a conversation into. The built-in set; the
workspace's own streams come later.

Verb.description: What an ask of the reader is: do something, or pay something.
